messages:
Noah: heads-up, eu-west prometheus remote_write p95 spiked ~10x about 10m ago, lots of timeouts and queue drops. @oncall?
Clara: which cluster/stack? screenshot of the alert?
Noah: eu-west-prod; alert: remote_write_send_failures > 3% for 5m. Logs show a bunch of http2 closed streams and queue overflow. pasted logs: ```May 18 10:12:34 prom-w-02 prometheus[1234]: ts=2026-05-18T10:12:34Z caller=remote.go:300 component=remote queue=default warning="dropping samples, queue full"
May 18 10:12:35 prom-w-02 prometheus[1234]: ts=2026-05-18T10:12:35Z caller=client.go:210 component=remote remote_write error="write tcp 10.12.1.5:50234->35.189.10.12:443: write: broken pipe"```
Aryan: hmm could be multiplexing getting stuck on an HTTP/2 connection to the remote endpoint (we recently changed the envoy egress config). Check envoy max_concurrent_streams and idle timeouts, those will bite long-lived streams.
Clara: we did roll forward envoy 1.24 -> 1.25 for egress yesterday, but only in eu-west. rolling back now?
dev-bot: deploy notice: rollout started for env/egress-proxy eu-west at 2026-05-18T09:55:12Z (change: envoy 1.25)
Rachael: also seeing a cardinality spike on gpu metrics around the same time — device_serial labels exploded. that will massively increase samples and blow queues. sample: `gpu_temp{device_serial="SN-ABC-12345",pod="model-serving-12"}` and hundreds of unique device_serial values per scrape.
Noah: yeah counts look bad: prometheus TSDB mem series +120k in 10m. remote_write queues filled.
Aryan: Immediate mitigations: 1) rollback envoy or relax max_concurrent_streams to avoid head-of-line stalls, 2) increase remote_write queue_config backlog: `max_shards`, `max_samples_per_send`, and `min_shards` temporarily, 3) add relabeling to drop device_serial from GPU exporters to stop cardinality spike.
Clara: drafting relabel now, testing on canary. proposed relabel_config: ```- source_labels: [__name__, device_serial]
  regex: (gpu_temp);.*
  action: replace
  target_label: device_serial
  replacement: "REDACTED"```
Rachael: instead of replace maybe labeldrop for device_serial across gpu exporters: ```- regex: device_serial
  action: labeldrop``` That avoids fake values and saves bytes.
Aryan: also tune send_timeout & timeout: `send_timeout: 30s` -> `15s` to fail fast and free shards, and bump `queue_config: {max_shards: 300, min_shards: 50, max_samples_per_send: 5000}` for short term.
Noah: any cost impact? remote_write retries will spike egress and storage costs.
Rachael: yes, large — SLO alert for cost vs baseline already firing on Grafana billing panel. suggest temporary scrape interval increase for gpu exporter from 15s -> 60s as emergency throttle.
Clara: rolling rollback envoy in eu-west now and applying labeldrop relabel to canary cluster.
dev-bot: rollout complete: env/egress-proxy eu-west rolled back to envoy 1.24 at 2026-05-18T10:32:21Z
Noah: canary relabel applied, metrics look sane on canary, queue drain started.
Aryan: follow-ups: add automated integration test for egress HTTP2 concurrency with remote_write endpoint, add a guarded relabel rule in base prometheus helm chart to drop exporter-internal serials, update runbook for queue-overflow with exact commands.
Rachael: filed ticket INF-2481 with next steps + cost estimate and dashboard panels to monitor series count, queue_length, remote_write_errors.
Noah: nice work, thanks. please add a short postmortem to the ticket once stable. :thumbsup:
